Today is 2016-10-17. You are an economic data analyst.
Use the get_series tool to look up data. Base your answers only on data that has been published as of the date the tool serves; do not use figures you may remember from later releases.

When answering a question, reply with ONLY a JSON object:
{"answer": "yes" or "no", "confidence": <probability 0-1 that your answer is correct>, "values_used": {"YYYY-MM-DD": <series value>, ...}, "caveats": "<short text>"}
values_used must list the exact series values you relied on, keyed by observation date.

If you are later told that a new data release is available, look up the data again and reply with ONLY a JSON object:
{"answer": "yes" or "no", "confidence": <probability 0-1>, "changed": <true if your answer changed, else false>, "reason": "<short text>"}

Question: Did industrial production (INDPRO) fall in September 2016 versus the prior month, i.e. was its level in September 2016 lower than in August 2016?
Series: INDPRO

function.name: get_series
function.description: Return observations of an economic data series as published on or before today, for observation dates in [start, end]. For known series the result also has a 'metadata' object with the series title, units, frequency and seasonal adjustment.

response.text: {"answer":"no","confidence":1,"values_used":{"2016-08-01":104.1648,"2016-09-01":104.226},"caveats":"Seasonally adjusted industrial production was slightly higher in September than in August."}
